title: The Cardinal Rule of Behavior Change
coreMove: Give the good habit an immediate satisfying signal while its larger payoff is still delayed.
sourcePressure: Behavior that feels satisfying now is more likely to be repeated, so good habits need some immediate reinforcement while bad habits often win because they reward immediately.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Confusing lasting reward with immediate satisfaction, or making rewards so large they become the habit.

hook: starting with a definition of cardinal rule
counterintuition: the problem is not motivation alone

exampleSpecs.domain: an ICU nurse rewarding hydration with a bead moved across her badge lanyard
exampleSpecs.audience: a shift worker who cannot feel long-term benefits at 4 p.m.
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a tiny immediate signal keeps the habit alive
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: after finishing the bottle, she slides one bead to the other side and feels the small click before the headache would have improved
exampleSpecs.firstImage: clear beads threaded on a blue badge lanyard

exampleSpecs.domain: a freelance illustrator making tax transfers satisfying with a visible progress stamp
exampleSpecs.audience: a self-employed creative tempted by immediate purchases
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the boring transfer gets a present-tense payoff
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she transfers 18 percent and stamps the invoice paid-to-future before opening any shopping tab
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a rubber stamp hovering over a paid invoice

exampleSpecs.domain: a widower walking to the corner mailbox for the sound of a brass token drop
exampleSpecs.audience: an older adult whose health payoff feels too far away
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the immediate sound becomes what the body repeats
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he drops a brass token into a jar only after returning from the mailbox, and the sound becomes the reward
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a brass token pinched above a glass jar on a hallway shelf

exampleSpecs.domain: a line cook studying food-safety cards to reveal one sticker on a knife-roll map
exampleSpecs.audience: an adult learner with failed exams behind him
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the visible reveal beats the distant promise of certification
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: his sister says the sticker is childish, then hears him admit the reveal is why he opened the cards
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a knife roll with one blank square on a taped map

exampleSpecs.domain: a city bus driver logging calm handoffs with a punched transit ticket
exampleSpecs.audience: a parent whose relationship payoff will lag
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the immediate punch keeps the new response alive before his daughter warms
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: after one calm doorway exchange, he punches a paper ticket and files it in the visor
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a paper transit ticket sliding into a visor clip

exampleSpecs.domain: a plant nursery worker rewarding sunscreen use by clicking a row counter
exampleSpecs.audience: an outdoor worker who never sees the prevented burn today
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether immediate tactile feedback reinforces the delayed-protection habit
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she applies sunscreen, clicks the counter once, and later sees the click mattered more than the health warning
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a metal row counter beside a sunscreen pump

skillTargets: design immediate satisfaction for delayed-payoff habits
predict why bad habits win in the present

tryThisNowSpec: Give one delayed-payoff habit a tiny immediate completion signal you can see, hear, or feel today.
